content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The strongest rival reading treats the formula as a broad image of anguish, remorse, or suffering under judgment, without making hostility toward the righteous its defining feature. That reading fits the weeping, exclusion, darkness, and judgment settings, but it explains the particular act of gnashing less precisely. Psalm 37:12 and Acts 7:54 directly portray gnashing as hostile fury against a righteous person, while Psalm 112:10 joins seeing the blessed, grief, gnashing, and perishing in one sequence. Luke 13:28 then supplies the closest Gospel correspondence: the excluded see the patriarchs in the kingdom and weep and gnash. These converging details make rage at the righteous—especially upon seeing their blessed standing—the better explanation of the gnashing itself. support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.
